summary: Morbidly obese man with CAD s/p CABG, chronic systolic heart failure (EF ~30%), type 2 diabetes and CKD was admitted electively to Urology for an 8 cm left renal mass and underwent laparoscopic left radical nephrectomy with retroperitoneal (para-aortic and hilar) lymph node dissection. Postoperative course was unremarkable apart from anemia (Hgb 8.5–8.9, Hct 26–28), creatinine rising to 2.0–2.3 mg/dL above his prior 1.3–1.6 baseline, and one markedly elevated glucose of 566 mg/dL. He was discharged tolerating diet, ambulating, voiding, on oral analgesia. The principal condition for this stay is the renal malignancy that prompted surgery, with post-nephrectomy renal insufficiency, anemia and diabetic hyperglycemia as secondary/complication codes.
most_likely: Malignant neoplasm of left kidney (renal cell carcinoma) treated with radical nephrectomy

differential.diagnosis: Malignant neoplasm of left kidney (renal cell carcinoma), 8 cm mass
supporting_evidence: Chief complaint: 8 cm left renal mass
Laparoscopic left radical nephrectomy plus retroperitoneal lymph node dissection
Prior ICD C649 malignant neoplasm of kidney
opposing_evidence: Final pathology not stated in redacted note
differential.reasoning: Elective admission solely for definitive oncologic resection of a suspicious renal mass; radical nephrectomy with nodal dissection makes renal malignancy the principal diagnosis.

differential.diagnosis: Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease following nephrectomy
supporting_evidence: Prior baseline creatinine 1.3–1.6, known CKD/diabetic nephropathy
Loss of one kidney after radical nephrectomy
opposing_evidence: Urine output maintained >30 cc/hr; trend improving at discharge
differential.reasoning: Postoperative creatinine clearly exceeds documented baseline in a solitary-kidney state, supporting acute renal insufficiency superimposed on CKD.

supporting_evidence: Hgb 8.5–8.9 g/dL, Hct 26.3–28.3 after major laparoscopic resection
opposing_evidence: No transfusion documented; no hematoma on exam
High RDW may suggest chronic component
differential.reasoning: Significant hemoglobin drop from prior baseline in the immediate postoperative period after nephrectomy and node dissection is typical acute blood-loss anemia.

differential.diagnosis: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia and diabetic chronic kidney disease
supporting_evidence: Glucose 566 mg/dL on one postoperative day; 113 on others
PMH non-insulin-dependent diabetes; prior ICD E1122
opposing_evidence: No documented ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar state
No diabetes medications on admission list
differential.reasoning: A marked perioperative hyperglycemic excursion in a known diabetic with CKD supports coding diabetes with hyperglycemia as an active secondary condition.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
supporting_evidence: Home torsemide, spironolactone, carvedilol, hydralazine, isosorbide continued
opposing_evidence: No edema on exam; no documented decompensation this stay
differential.reasoning: Chronic, medically managed HFrEF requiring careful perioperative fluid management—relevant comorbidity but not decompensated during this admission.

differential.diagnosis: Coronary artery disease in patient with prior coronary artery bypass graft
supporting_evidence: Prior ICD Z951 presence of aortocoronary bypass graft; on aspirin, statin
opposing_evidence: No chest pain, ischemic events or troponins this stay
differential.reasoning: Documented ischemic heart disease increases perioperative risk and is codable as a chronic comorbidity/status.

differential.diagnosis: Morbid obesity with obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP
supporting_evidence: PMH morbid obesity and OSA on CPAP; prior ICD Z6841, G4733
opposing_evidence: No respiratory events documented this admission
differential.reasoning: Objective BMI in the class III range with documented OSA supports secondary coding and affects perioperative risk.

differential.diagnosis: Essential hypertension with hypertensive chronic kidney disease
supporting_evidence: PMH hypertension; on losartan, carvedilol, hydralazine, isosorbide
opposing_evidence: Blood pressures not recorded in current structured data
differential.reasoning: Chronic hypertension with renal involvement is well documented historically and continued pharmacologically, though not actively managed as a problem this stay.

rule_outs.why: Hemoglobin low but stable; exam shows no hematoma collection, drains removed without difficulty.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Surgical site or urinary tract infection
rule_outs.why: WBC normal at 8.3, incisions clean/dry/intact, only prophylactic antibiotics given.
No dyspnea, no edema, no pulmonary edema imaging this stay despite EF ~30% history.
No calf tenderness or edema; pneumoboots prophylaxis, no symptoms documented.
Single glucose of 566 with normal sodium, anion gap 18, bicarbonate 23 and no altered mental status documented.

uncertain_areas: Surgical pathology (RCC subtype, stage, nodal involvement) would confirm the malignancy code and laterality
Whether creatinine elevation was documented as acute kidney injury versus expected post-nephrectomy CKD progression
Whether anemia was labeled acute blood loss versus chronic disease; transfusion records unavailable
Whether the glucose 566 was treated as a coded hyperglycemia/HHS event or a lab artifact
Perioperative vitals and any cardiac monitoring results that could indicate arrhythmia or heart failure exacerbation
